# Inventory Costing

⚠️ **Finance warning / Avertissement finance** : informational only, not investment advice. Inventory is usually the largest number a reviewer will challenge: absorbing overhead at the wrong capacity inflates unit costs and profit, a skipped write-down overstates assets, there is a real risk of loss in any reporting or pricing decision taken from wrong unit costs, and no output here is a promise of return. Curated by Skill Harbor: the inventory costing skill of GAJETOso/financeskills. Use it to value inventory, choose or apply a costing method, or handle write-downs under IAS 2 or ASC 330. The opening profile separates raw materials, work in progress, finished goods, spares and goods in transit (checked against shipping terms), names the method in use (FIFO, periodic or moving weighted average, standard cost, retail method, with LIFO flagged as US GAAP only and prohibited under IFRS), and fixes the cost components: purchase cost net of discounts and rebates plus import duties, non-recoverable taxes and freight in, conversion costs with fixed overhead absorbed at normal capacity, and the excluded list (abnormal waste, storage of finished goods, selling costs, administrative overhead, foreign exchange losses). The mechanics are explicit: FIFO sends the oldest costs to cost of sales and leaves inventory at recent costs, the moving weighted average recomputes after each receipt, and the same formula must apply to all inventories of a similar nature and use.
